# @k8ordo/framework

> Turns `src/routes/` into an application of React Server Components, built
> with Vite, in one of two modes chosen in `vite.config.ts`:
> `framework({ mode: 'static' })` renders every route at build time into
> files a static host serves, with no server, and
> `framework({ mode: 'server' })` renders per request on a server. Switching
> is changing `mode` (and dropping `paths`, `site` and `csp`, which server
> mode refuses); nothing else in the application
> changes. Pick `server` when the application needs the request — Server
> Actions, `guard.ts`, the `request` prop, cookies, a page that exports
> `search`, parameter values with no list rendered on the server (static
> mode has only a `fallback.tsx`'s shell for those, drawn in the browser) —
> and `static` otherwise; static mode refuses all of those by name, in the
> build and in `vite dev` (`this application wants mode: 'server'`).
> `src/routes/` is the pathname space and holds nothing else
> (page/layout/not-found/error/loading/fallback/redirect/guard/route files,
> `[param]` and `(group)` directories; `_` is an ordinary character in
> a segment and a name starting with `.` is not read, so `/.well-known` cannot
> be a route; components live outside it in `src/components/` and every
> other module in `src/lib/`); a page or layout may
> `export const paramsSchema` (any Standard Schema, synchronous) to type its
> parameters — a refused value makes the pattern not answer, so the walk goes
> on to `not-found.tsx` — a page that says `notFound()` is answered by the
> nearest `not-found.tsx`, an `error.tsx` shows in place of what throws below
> it, a `loading.tsx` shows while what is below it suspends, a `redirect.ts`
> answers 307/308 (server) or is written as a page that sends the visitor on
> (static), and a `route.ts` answers its URL with a `Response` (server: every
> method it exports; static: written as the file its `GET` answers). Under
> server mode a Server Action ends with `redirect()`, a `guard.ts` runs before
> whatever answers below it, `cookies()` reads and writes cookies, and a page
> receives `request`. Static mode lists parameter values with `paths` —
> beside a `fallback.tsx`, the values it does not list get a shell: the
> layouts written as HTML, the page drawn in the browser from the URL, and a
> `_redirects` (or `vercel()`'s routes) through which a host reaches it —
> writes `404.html` and `sitemap.xml`, and puts a Content-Security-Policy in
> a `<meta>` by hash (`csp`). Application code imports from `@k8ordo/framework`
> (the router's `href`, `notFound`, `PageProps`, …); `@k8ordo/router` is a
> required peer but never named. Boundaries are React's own `'use client'`
> with `server-only` modules barred from the client bundle, and the route
> table and type wiring are generated rather than hand-written.
>
> Like every k8ordo package it assumes React 19 and Server Components, uses
> only what has reached Baseline newly available, and ships no polyfills or
> legacy fallbacks.

When installed via npm, these docs live under `node_modules/@k8ordo/framework/docs/`.
Start with GUIDE.md, then follow the reference most relevant to the task.

## Guide

- [Design Guide](GUIDE.md): choosing a mode and what static mode refuses,
  setup (install, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, the root layout as the
  document), `vite dev` and `vite preview` against a static build, the
  entries, and the plugin's options.

## References

- [Routing](references/routing.md): the `routes/` grammar and every refusal
  the build names, where a `fallback.tsx` may sit, how a page is sent in
  each mode, `loading.tsx`, `route.ts` (methods and `405` under server
  mode, a file under static mode), the generated `.k8ordo/` files (the
  route table, and the `Register`s: the table's, and `@k8ordo/i18n`'s when
  `src/i18n.ts` exports `locales` by name), titles,
  and fetching the next page ahead (`data-k8ordo-prefetch`).
- [Parameters](references/params.md): `paramsSchema` — a refused value is a
  pathname the pattern does not answer — and, under static mode, the `paths`
  option: supplying pathnames, expanding a parameter every page shares, and
  what fails the build; and `fallback.tsx` for the values it does not list —
  the shell it renders (no props, the layouts' schemas only, the shell's
  `pathname`), shell locations in `paths` and the parameters a layout above
  forces them to fill, reading the value in the browser with `useMatch`,
  `notFound()` shown in place, routes below its parameter, and what it
  costs.
- [Errors and redirects](references/errors.md): `error.tsx`, a Server
  Component that throws stopping a static build, `notFound()` and
  `not-found.tsx` (a document waits for its page under server mode; under a
  `fallback.tsx`, shown in place), and `redirect.ts` in each mode.
- [Execution boundaries](references/boundaries.md): `'use client'`,
  `use(browser())` for a component that needs a browser (and `useMatch` /
  `usePathname` waiting for it on their own under a `fallback.tsx`),
  `server-only` modules, the search — `@k8ordo/state`'s, or handed to a
  page that exports `search` under server mode — and forms.
- [Server Actions](references/actions.md): server mode only. `'use server'`
  against `server-only`, `cookies()` / `responseHeaders()` /
  `requestHeaders()` in an action, the page context an action runs in, forms
  before JavaScript, and ending with `redirect()`.
- [Guards, cookies and the request](references/guards.md): server mode only.
  `guard.ts` (outer first; a `Response` ends the request),
  `responseHeaders()`, `cookies()` and its defaults, and the read-only
  `request` a page receives.
- [Content Security Policy](references/csp.md): `nonce()` in a header a
  guard writes under server mode; the `csp` option and
  `colorSchemeScriptHash()` under static mode, and `connect-src` for the
  data a `fallback.tsx`'s shell fetches.
- [Running and deploying](references/deploy.md): a static build's
  `dist/client/` (HTML, `index.rsc` payloads, shells, `404.html`,
  `sitemap.xml`, `_redirects`), the rewrites that reach a shell on Netlify,
  Cloudflare Workers static assets (`html_handling`, the 2,000/100 rule
  limits) and Pages, Vercel and any other host, and `serve` and
  `vite preview` serving a static build as a static host;
  under server mode, a `dist/` that runs on its own with
  `node dist/server.js` (`PORT`, `HOST`, every dependency bundled in, and
  `resolve.external` for one that cannot be), `serve` (compression, `ETag`,
  `Range`), the request handler under Node.js, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare
  Workers, the same-origin rule for a `POST`, and `vercel()` in either mode;
  a tab opened before a deploy, and Vite's `base`.

## Entry points

- `@k8ordo/framework` — what application code imports, re-exported from
  `@k8ordo/router` (which stays a peer, one copy): `href`, `navigateTo`,
  `bindParams`, `notFound`, `isNotFound`, `usePathname`,
  `usePendingPathname`, `useMatch`, `matchPath`, `normalizePathname`,
  `withBase`, and the types `PageProps`, `LayoutProps`, `RouteContext`,
  `ErrorProps`, `BoundLinks`, `BoundParams`, `MatchablePattern`,
  `MatchOptions`, `NavigateToOptions` and the `Registered*` types. Not
  `useParams` or `useRoute`: a page receives `params` as a prop.
- `@k8ordo/framework/vite` — `framework(options)` returns the Vite plugins;
  `options.mode` (`'static' | 'server'`) is required, `options.routesDir`
  moves the route directory (default `src/routes`). Only with
  `mode: 'static'`: `options.paths` supplies concrete pathnames for routes
  with parameters (a parameterised route left uncovered fails the build,
  unless its page has a `fallback.tsx`), and for such a page also shell
  locations, pathnames that still hold the parameters left to the browser
  (`/ja/posts/:id`), `options.site` (the origin) makes the build also write
  `sitemap.xml`, and
  `options.csp` (directives → sources, `ContentSecurityPolicy`) is the
  Content-Security-Policy written into each page's `<meta>`, first in
  `<head>`, with the hashes of the framework's own inline scripts on that
  page added to `script-src` (or `default-src` made into it) and
  `script-src-elem`; a policy with `'strict-dynamic'`, `frame-ancestors`,
  `report-uri` or `sandbox` is refused. `FrameworkOptions` is
  `StaticOptions | ServerOptions`. This entry loads Vite and is for
  `vite.config.ts` only.
- `@k8ordo/framework/server` — server mode only; a static build refuses any
  module that imports a value from it. What code inside the request handler
  imports, needing nothing from Node but `AsyncLocalStorage`: `redirect(to)`
  ends a Server Action by sending the visitor to `to`; `responseHeaders()`
  is the `Headers` the final response carries, `cookies()` the request's
  cookies to read and write (`get`, `has`, `set(name, value,
  CookieOptions)`, `delete(name, CookieScope)`; defaults `path: '/'`,
  `httpOnly`, `secure` (not over plain HTTP to `localhost`),
  `sameSite: 'lax'`; every write a `Set-Cookie` on the answer), and
  `requestHeaders()` the headers the request arrived with — all three from
  a `guard.ts`, a `route.ts` or a Server Action, and they throw anywhere
  else; `nonce()` is the nonce this answer's inline scripts carry, new per
  request and readable anywhere the request is answered, the render
  included; `Guard<P>` is the type of what a `guard.ts` default-exports
  (`({ request, params }) => Response | void`) and `GuardContext<P>` its
  argument; `RedirectTarget` is the type of what a `redirect.ts`
  default-exports, and `RouteRequest` the type of the `request` prop.
- `@k8ordo/framework/serve` — the Node.js server for a build.
  `serve({ dist?, port?, host? })` (`ServeOptions`: `dist` defaults to
  `dist` under the working directory, `port` to `3000`, `host` to
  `localhost`) serves a build and returns a `Server`, `{ port, url, close }`
  (`port: 0` takes a free port): for a server build, the client build's
  files as they are and everything else through the request handler; for a
  static build, as a static host does — files, the `_redirects` rewrites,
  `404.html` under 404, never the handler. `dist/server.js` runs it under
  server mode; a server of your own imports it, with `@k8ordo/framework` in
  `dependencies`.
- `dist/server.js` — under server mode, what the build writes to start
  `serve` on the build it sits in: `node dist/server.js`, listening on
  `PORT` (default `3000`) and `HOST` (default `localhost`), closing and
  exiting with `0` on `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`. `serve` and every
  dependency of the handler are bundled into `dist/`, with
  `dist/package.json` (written in either mode) marking it ES modules, so
  `dist/` runs with nothing installed and the framework is a dev
  dependency.
- `dist/rsc/index.js` — under server mode, the built request handler, a
  plain `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>` default export with every
  dependency bundled in, that needs nothing from its runtime but
  `AsyncLocalStorage` (`node:async_hooks`), so Node.js, Bun, Deno and
  Cloudflare Workers with `nodejs_compat` run it directly; the host serves
  `dist/client/` in front of it.
- `@k8ordo/framework/vercel` — `vercel()` returns a Vite plugin to put
  beside `framework()`, in either mode: `vite build` then also writes
  `.vercel/output/` (Build Output API v3) for `vercel build` /
  `vercel deploy --prebuilt` — the client build as static files at Vite's
  `base` (`assets/` immutable), and under server mode the request handler
  as one streaming Node.js function; under static mode no function, and the
  shells' rewrites as routes tried after the files, then `404.html`.
- `@k8ordo/framework/generated` — what the generated `.k8ordo/` files
  import (`defineRoutes`, `Register`, …). Not for code written by hand.
